item.title: The Future of AI Cryptanalysis
item.description: <p>Matthew Green <a href="https://x.com/matthew_d_green/status/2107992246360649879">has</a> <a href="https://x.com/matthew_d_green/status/2108278850555674975?s=46">been</a> <a href="https://x.com/matthew_d_green/status/2108552414978564418">writing</a> a rather pessimistic series of posts about the potential for AI systems to vastly outperform humans in cryptanalysis of both symmetric and public-key ciphers.</p> <p>I am more optimistic than he is. That is, I have stronger faith in the over-engineering cryptographers tend to do. I am trying to write this up in more detail.</p>

item.title: curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution
item.description:
A flaw in how curl handles HTTP/2 uploads lets a malicious server receiving an upload corrupt the client's memory, and the researcher who reported it turned that into code execution on the uploading machine.
The curl project fixed it on October 14 in&nbsp;curl 8.23.0. Taking over a client needs exact knowledge of its build and memory layout, and curl expects a real attack to end in a crash
